_comment2_undeclared_live_roots: The MIRROR half, added 2026-08-19. The rest of this file is about a DECLARED root that stopped resolving. This half is about a LIVE root nobody declared - the same shrink arriving from the other side, and the worse one, because a dead root at least leaves a trace in the policy while an undeclared root leaves nothing at all and no ratchet makes it awkward. Mechanism: a declaration SITE (one array, keyed policy_file::json_pointer) is ROOT-ENUMERATING when at least ROOT_ENUMERATION_MIN_HITS=2 of its entries are root references into the live universe; such a site owes the WHOLE universe, and every live root it omits is an undeclared_live_root. WHAT EXISTS is derived, never enumerated here: governance/capability-registry.json (the ADR-0562 closed registry) intersected with what is on disk, plus carried_legacy_roots. Deriving it is the entire point - a capability that lands is expected everywhere BY CONSTRUCTION, with no edit to this file, exactly as the root Cargo.toml's four shape globs made a conforming capability a workspace member by construction after its 24 per-capability globs had turned the member array into a mutex every reorg move serialized on. Registry names supply VOCABULARY and the filesystem supplies LIVENESS: `policy` is registered with no directory, and demanding a root that does not exist would be dead_scan_root issued as an order. baselined_undeclared_live_roots is FROZEN, shrink-only and TWO-SIDED (frozen_undeclared_baseline_is_exactly_the_live_gap_set): a new gap is blocking, and a gap that CLOSES must be un-frozen in the same change, because a one-sided ceiling cannot tell a widened gate from a collapsed collector. It is a SET of named keys and not a count, so closing it is a reviewable diff.
_comment: Scan-root liveness. Every COVERAGE-BEARING root a gate policy declares must resolve to a real path (or, for a glob, match at least one). A dead root means the gate scans less than it claims and reports GREEN over an empty set - and because the fleet's anti-narrowing ratchet forbids REMOVING a root, a reorg move that empties one leaves it permanently dead AND unremovable. Keys are the FULL JSON POINTER, not the leaf name: `roots` appears at three different nesting levels inside rust-first-automation-policy.json alone, so leaf-name keying would collapse distinct declarations and let one baselined entry silently tolerate another. Only coverage-bearing keys are in scope; vocabulary lists (exclude_prefixes, allowed_paths, forbidden_prefixes) are excluded because a dead entry there excludes or permits nothing. forward_declarations hold paths declared deliberately BEFORE they exist - flagging those would punish declaring a reorg destination ahead of the move - and a forward declaration whose path LANDS must be retired so it cannot become a permanent unaudited exemption. baselined_dead_roots is FROZEN and shrink-only.

_provenance.policy: shrink-only; a NEW dead root fails, and a landed forward declaration must be retired
_provenance._build_root_retired_2026_08_09: The three `::build` forward declarations (dto-authz-trust, embedded-asset-hermeticity, authz-coverage) were RETIRED here because build/ landed its first crate — build/port-engine/core/port-engine-kernel, PR #1621 — which is verbatim the event their own reason strings named (`Created when build/ lands its first crate`). Retirement is a DELETION FROM THIS EXEMPTION MAP ONLY: `build` stays in all three policies' scan_roots arrays untouched, and now resolves, so it is a live audited root rather than an unaudited standing exemption. That is the whole point of forward_declarations being pinned by forward_declarations_are_all_still_absent: a declaration whose path arrives must stop being tolerated in the same change that makes it real. Sibling roots base/ and policy/ remain absent and remain declared; whoever lands their first crate owes the same one-line retirement. app/ was later retired in _app_root_retired_2026_08_11. NOT retired here: module-membership declared no `build` entry, so it had nothing to retire.
_provenance._build_widening_measured_2026_08_09: The widening is not free of consequence and was measured rather than assumed. embedded-asset-hermeticity now walks build/, and the new crate carries four include_str! sites (src/lib.rs:78 `lib.rs`, src/lib.rs:93 `../tests/seams.rs`, tests/neutrality.rs:42 `../src/lib.rs`, tests/neutrality.rs:48 `seams.rs`). All four resolve inside targets whose BUCK srcs already provide them — the library globs `src/**/*.rs` plus `tests/seams.rs`, and the neutrality test globs all three — so the gate stays green with no baseline movement. caller-supplied-authorization and endpoint-authorization-coverage now walk build/ too; the kernel exposes no DTO deserialization and no HTTP endpoint, so both are likewise zero-delta. Verified by running all three gates, not by reading the policies.
_provenance._app_root_retired_2026_08_11: The four `::app` forward declarations (dto-authz-trust, embedded-asset-hermeticity, authz-coverage, module-membership) were RETIRED here because app/ landed its first tracked path — app/README.md on integ/app (PR #1668, OVERRULE 3d glue-only). Retirement is a DELETION FROM THIS EXEMPTION MAP ONLY: `app` stays in each policy's scan_roots arrays untouched, and now resolves, so it is a live audited root. README-only (zero crates) keeps hermeticity/authz widening zero-delta. Sibling roots base/ and policy/ remain absent and remain declared.
_provenance._coverage_keys_widened_2026_08_19: MEASURED, not assumed. `governed_roots` was added to coverage_bearing_keys because two live gate policies were outside this gate's universe entirely: canonical-json declares `governed_roots` and product-protocol-policy declares it nested under `manifest_inventory`. Before: 202 declared roots across 7 policy files and 12 declaration sites. After: 225 roots across 9 files and 14 sites - and note the pre-existing `declared_roots_total: 200` in this same block was already two stale, which is the drift this crate exists to catch, in this crate. Both newly covered files' roots RESOLVE, so the dead-root baseline is unchanged at eleven. NOT added: `manifest_inventory`. It is an OBJECT everywhere it occurs, never an array, so the collector could never match it; a key that cannot fire is dead vocabulary and is indistinguishable from a working entry, which is the same false assurance as a dead scan root. If it ever becomes an array, add it then.
_provenance._collector_fail_closed_measured_2026_08_: The collector's `let Ok(gate_dirs) = read_dir(ci/facade) else { return Observed::default() }` is now a panic naming the path, and the reason is MEASURED rather than argued. Pointing that read at an absent directory on the pre-change code left live_corpus_is_green_against_the_frozen_policy - the assertion carrying this gate's VERDICT - GREEN over a corpus of zero. min_expected_roots did not object either at floor 0; what failed were three collateral fidelity checks, and every one of them instructed the reader to `remove it from baselined_dead_roots`, which is a remediation that would have made the vacuous gate permanently green. Same treatment for an unreadable gate directory, and min_expected_live_roots closes the matching hole in the new undeclared-root code: an unloadable capability registry would otherwise make every declaration site trivially complete.
_provenance._undeclared_root_baseline_frozen_2026_08: 96 undeclared_live_root gaps across 9 of the 14 declaration sites, frozen against a 32-root universe (29 registered-and-on-disk, plus the 4 carried legacy roots, minus third-party/). They are DEBT MADE VISIBLE, not tolerated design, and they are the work queue for the per-gate widening: embedded-asset-hermeticity misses 19 live roots including comms/ (24 crate directories - a dangling embedded asset planted there was mutation-proven GREEN); product-protocol-policy misses 11; automation-language-policy's cli_package_authority misses 29 and interpreter_command_authority 28, both scanning for classes (a `-cli` package name, a spawned python/node) that can be born under any capability; layer-dependency-acyclicity misses app/, infra/ and kernel/ while still carrying the 31-glob per-capability form the root Cargo.toml retired. Each entry is a named key, so each widening is a reviewable deletion from this list. Nothing here was tuned green: the only root removed from the universe is third-party/, under universe_exclusions, because it is vendored upstream source the repo does not author.
_provenance._cloud_root_retired_2026_08_17: The top-level cloud/ tree is intentionally retired, but its seven remaining coverage-bearing declarations stay in their owning policies so future reintroduction is scanned immediately and anti-narrowing cannot be bypassed as cleanup. Those exact fully qualified declarations move into the frozen shrink-only baseline; the live exact-set test binds the baseline to all and only currently dead non-forward roots.

oya.deletion_condition: Delete this entry when the last oya/<service>/crates/ crate has been moved under ADR-0562 and the oya/ directory no longer exists. Until then oya/ holds the bulk of the un-migrated fleet, and a gate that does not scan it is blind to most of the repo.

libs.deletion_condition: Delete this entry when libs/ has been consolidated into base/ and the capability faces per ADR-0562 and the directory no longer exists. libs/oya-* is still a live crate root today.

tools.deletion_condition: Delete this entry when the tools/ removal-candidate root is gone (ADR-0701). It still holds tools/oya-* crates and repo automation that the language and tier gates must see.

infra.deletion_condition: Delete this entry when infra/ has finished draining into k8s/ and iac/ and the directory no longer exists. It is the live GitOps and external-secrets surface today, so it is first-party ground a gate must not skip.

third-party.reason: reindeer-vendored upstream crate sources (the buck2 cell root third-party//, top-level per the ADR-0615 amendment). It owns zero first-party crates and the repo does not author its contents, so a gate widened into it would lint code nobody here can fix. This is a category error, not deferred work: unlike every entry in baselined_undeclared_live_roots, no future change is supposed to make a gate scan it.

ci/facade/embedded-asset-hermeticity/emb.reason: Same pre-widening as app/ above; base/ is the ADR-0562 shared floor and an embedded asset there must be BUCK-srcs-mapped like any other. Created by the first libs/ consolidation move.

Same pre-widening as app/ above. The policy capability (ADR-0615, extracted from iam) will expose policy-decision endpoints; an unauthenticated control plane there is the worst case this gate exists to block.

ci/facade/module-membership/capability-m.reason: ADR-0562 capability-first destination for the shared floor. Declared ahead of creation for the same reason as app/; created by the first libs/ consolidation move.

Declared capability in the ADR-0562 closed registry with no directory yet; created when the policy-pack capability lands its first crate. This membership `scan_roots` forward declaration is SOUND and stays: scan_roots is pure coverage, so naming a not-yet-existing root costs nothing and the root is walked the moment it appears. Its tier-policy twin (`crate_root_globs::policy/*/*`) was RETIRED 2026-08-01 because the tier policy gives no such free ride: every crate_root_globs root must also appear in service_roots/capability_roots/unclassified_roots (pinned by every_governed_glob_root_is_declared_in_the_policy), and for a crate-less `policy` the only reachable option was `unclassified_roots`, a live SKIP-ALL-EDGES exemption that R6b correctly REDs. The forward declaration therefore structurally required a standing violation to exist, which is why it was baselined rather than fixed. Re-add the glob together with a real root declaration in the same change that lands policy/'s first crate — the ADR-0615 re-home of the nine iam-mapped Cedar/PDP crates, filed separately as a MOVE.
